content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm looking for ideas on this issue: Inputs: I1 = Start 1 I2 = Start 2 I3 = Start 3 I4 = Start 4 I5 = Stop all Outputs: Q1 = Command 1 Q2 = Command 2 Q3 = Command 3 Q4 = Command 4 Logic requirement: - On the first cycle, I1 triggers Q1, I2 triggers Q2, I3 triggers Q3, and I4 triggers Q4. - I5 stops all motors. - On the second cycle, I1 triggers Q2, I2 triggers Q3, I3 triggers Q4, and I4 triggers Q1. - The cycles keep alternating among four motors. Any suggestions or ideas? Thanks and Best Regards [user_name]
If this is only about switching between four motors, why do you need advice? Are the start inputs (I1-I4) and the stop input (I5) fixed or do they change dynamically?

Thank you for replying! I'm asking for ideas because I believe forums are for sharing experiences. There are always many ways to solve an issue, and someone with more background might have a better solution. Of course, no one is forced to respond. Back to the main point, the logic to implement would look like this: - On power up - Q1 is activated by a Set/Reset function SET I1 - RESET I5 - Q2 is activated by a Set/Reset function SET I2 - RESET I5 - Q3 is activated by a Set/Reset function SET I3 - RESET I5 - Q4 is activated by a Set/Reset function SET I4 - RESET I5 - When I5 is pressed, all Q outputs turn off, and when I5 goes to zero, motor commands change as follows: - Q1 is triggered by SET I4 - RESET I5 - Q2 is triggered by SET I1 - RESET I5 - Q3 is triggered by SET I2 - RESET I5 - Q4 is triggered by SET I3 - RESET I5 - And so on My initial idea: - Keep count of powered Q outputs - Use four memory words MW, set to 1, 2, 3, 4 at startup - Use these MWs to compare current active Q and activate accordingly - When I5 is activated, cycle MW values from 2, 3, 4, 1 I feel there could be more efficient options out there... Thanks and Best Regards [user_name]
If you're after a more efficient method, you should develop your own solution, not just in text but also in program form.
No problem. Seems like we have different views of what a forum is for.
It seems you don't have your own solution and are expecting the forum to provide completed work for you—even for what you consider a straightforward task involving the alternation of four motors.
Feel free to think as you like. Have a good evening.

analysis.insight_summary: The user describes a challenge in designing control logic for alternating four motor outputs and seeks ideas for a more effective solution. Discussion centers on logic design principles for programmable controllers, without focusing on specific products or providing direct solutions. The conversation highlights differences in expectations regarding collaborative problem-solving in forum environments.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants collaborative input and suggestions for optimizing the process of alternating four motor outputs through input commands. They hope to draw on others' experience to achieve a more efficient and refined logic than their initial concept.
